title: Module surjectivity on a principal open descends near its image under field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $\varphi:M\to N$ a $C$-linear map of arbitrary $C$-modules. Put $C_K=C\otimes_k K$ and $\varphi_K=\varphi\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_K$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $v\in C_K$ and let $P\subset C_K$ be a prime ideal with $v\notin P$, and put $\mathfrak p=\{c\in C:c\otimes1\in P\}$. If $(\varphi_K)_v:(M\otimes_k K)_v\to(N\otimes_k K)_v$ is surjective, then there exists $c\in C\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $\varphi_c:M_c\to N_c$ is surjective. Here a subscript $a$ denotes localization at $1,a,a^2,\ldots$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. No finite-generation hypothesis on either module or on $C$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $S=C\otimes_kK$ and let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be contraction. The affine fibre-product comparison identifies $\pi$ with the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Universal openness over a field therefore makes $U=\pi(D(v))$ open. Since $P\in D(v)$ and $\pi(P)=\mathfrak p$, the basic-open basis supplies $c\notin\mathfrak p$ with $D(c)\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), assertion (1), combined with Morphisms Tag 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open); agent-written module consequence

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\in D(c)$. Choose $Q\in D(v)$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$, as permitted by $D(c)\subseteq\pi(D(v))$. The field-extension map $C\to S$ is faithfully flat, hence flat. Localization at these corresponding primes gives a flat local homomorphism $A=C_{\mathfrak q}\to B=S_Q$. In particular it is faithfully flat and reflects surjectivity of module maps after tensoring with $B$. No finite-presentation hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), assertion (1), combined with Morphisms Tag 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open); agent-written module consequence

proof.text: For any $C$-module $E$ there is a natural $B$-linear identification $(E\otimes_kK)_Q\cong E_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_A B$. Explicitly, $(e\otimes\lambda)/t\mapsto(e/1)\otimes((1\otimes\lambda)/t)$, for $t\in S\setminus Q$. The inverse is $(e/s)\otimes b\mapsto b\,(e\otimes1)/(s\otimes1)$, for $s\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$. The denominators are invertible because $Q$ contracts to $\mathfrak q$; the formulas respect fraction equality and the tensor balancing relations. Their composites fix the displayed generators, so they are inverse. Replacing $e$ by $\varphi(e)$ shows that these identifications carry $(\varphi_K)_Q$ to $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_A1_B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), assertion (1), combined with Morphisms Tag 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open); agent-written module consequence

proof.text: Surjectivity of $(\varphi_K)_v$ implies surjectivity of $(\varphi_K)_Q$. Indeed, given $y/t$ in $(N\otimes_kK)_Q$, represent a preimage of $y/1$ in the $v$-localization by $x/v^a$. Equality there says $v^b(v^a y-\varphi_K(x))=0$ for some $b\geq0$. Since $v\notin Q$, this yields $\varphi_K(x)/(v^at)=y/t$ in the $Q$-localization. Thus the map identified in Step 3 is surjective. Faithfully flat reflection from Step 2 now gives surjectivity of $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ for every $\mathfrak q\in D(c)$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), assertion (1), combined with Morphisms Tag 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open); agent-written module consequence

proof.text: Put $T=N/\varphi(M)$. Localization exactness applied to $M\to N\to T\to0$ and the preceding surjectivity gives $T_{\mathfrak q}=0$ for all $\mathfrak q\in D(c)$. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C_c$ contracts to such a $\mathfrak q$, by the spectrum-of-localization comparison. Moreover $(T_c)_{\mathfrak n}\cong T_{\mathfrak q}$: the fraction map sends $(e/c^a)/(r/c^b)$ to $c^b e/(c^a r)$, with inverse $e/s\mapsto(e/1)/(s/1)$. Hence every maximal localization of $0\to T_c$ is bijective. The cited maximal-localization criterion gives $T_c=0$. Finally localization exactness in $M_c\to N_c\to T_c\to0$ gives surjectivity of $\varphi_c$, with $c\notin\mathfrak p$ as required.

lean.note: The canonical scalar-extension model (C ⊗[k] K) ⊗[C] M represents M ⊗[k] K via (c ⊗ λ) ⊗ m ↦ (c • m) ⊗ λ; under this identification LinearMap.baseChange is φ ⊗ id_K. No finiteness assumptions.
